notes: Do Now question bank (OCR J277). questions: style quiz (from past Do Now quizzes, tidied) or exam (new, modelled on OCR 2024/25 question types; never OCR wording). lang = python|erl for code. misc = misconception from OCR examiners' reports. Generators: reference in generators.py, port to JS; examples.json = test vectors.

questions.q: Define the term **decomposition**.
questions.ans: Breaking a large problem down into **smaller sub-problems** that are easier to solve.

questions.q: Define the term **abstraction**.
questions.ans: **Removing unnecessary detail** so you can focus on what is needed to solve the problem.

questions.q: Define the term **algorithm**.
questions.ans: A **sequence of steps** (instructions) to solve a problem.

questions.q: Copy and complete: "______ is when you break down a large problem into several smaller ___-______."
questions.ans: **Decomposition** … smaller **sub-problems**.

questions.q: Copy and complete: "An ______ is a series of ______ to solve a ______."
questions.ans: An **algorithm** is a series of **steps** to solve a **problem**.

questions.q: Copy and complete: "______ is when we remove all ______ details in order to solve a problem."
questions.ans: **Abstraction** … remove all **unnecessary** details.

questions.q: Is a recipe an example of an **algorithm** or **abstraction**? Explain.
questions.ans: **Algorithm**: it is a sequence of steps that solves a problem (making the dish).

questions.q: The London Tube map is a good example of an algorithm, abstraction or decomposition? Why?
questions.ans: **Abstraction**: it leaves out real distances, streets and bends, keeping only stations and connections.

questions.q: You are creating a new console game. How could you use **decomposition**? Name three sub-problems.
questions.ans: e.g. **player movement**, **scoring**, **levels/maps**, **menus**, **sound** (any 3 sensible parts).

questions.q: A chess club stores the **winner**, **loser** and **date** of each game. How has **abstraction** been used?
questions.ans: Only the details needed are stored; details like the **moves, weather or time taken** are left out.

questions.q: Explain how **abstraction** could be used in a program that calculates **taxi fares**.
questions.ans: Keep only **distance, time, number of passengers**; ignore car colour, driver name, the route taken.

questions.q: A sat-nav map shows roads but not buildings or trees. Which computational thinking technique is this? Explain.
questions.ans: **Abstraction**: removing detail not needed to find a route.

questions.q: One designer splits a game into **levels, menus and scoring**. Another leaves the **weather** out of a football game. Name each technique.
questions.ans: Splitting up = **decomposition**. Leaving out detail = **abstraction**.

questions.q: Draw the flowchart shape for a **decision**.
questions.ans: A **diamond**, with two exits (Yes / No).

questions.q: Draw the flowchart shape for a **process** (e.g. assigning a value to a variable).
questions.ans: A **rectangle**.

questions.q: Draw the flowchart shape for **input/output**.
questions.ans: A **parallelogram**.

questions.q: Name the flowchart shape for: a **decision**, **input/output**, a **process**. Why does a decision have two exits?
questions.ans: **Diamond**, **parallelogram**, **rectangle**. One exit for **True/Yes**, one for **False/No**.

questions.q: What will this OCR reference language code output?
questions.ans: **2** then **4** (the even numbers from 1 to 5).

questions.q: A program makes a username from the **first 3 letters of the first name** and the **first 2 of the surname**. What is the username for **Ada Lovelace**?
questions.ans: **AdaLo**

questions.q: What is the purpose of a **trace table**?
questions.ans: To **follow an algorithm step by step**, recording the value of each variable, to find errors or work out the output.

questions.q: Complete a trace table (i, output) for this algorithm.
questions.ans: i: 0 to 5. Output when i is 0, 2, 4: **P**, **R**, **O**.

questions.q: Complete a trace table (x, output) for this algorithm.
questions.ans: x = 0, 1, 2. Outputs **Saw**, **Sharks**, **Lion King**.

questions.q: This program should be FizzBuzz. What does it print when i is **15**, and why is it different from normal FizzBuzz?
questions.ans: **Fizz**: 15 % 3 == 0 is checked first, so the Buzz branch (and FizzBuzz) is never reached.

questions.q: What is the difference between a **logic error** and a **syntax error**? Give an example of each.
questions.ans: Syntax: breaks the language rules so it **won't run** (e.g. missing colon). Logic: **runs but gives the wrong result** (e.g. > instead of >=).

questions.q: If my program runs but produces an **unexpected result**, what kind of error is that?
questions.ans: A **logic error**.

questions.q: What is wrong with this Python code?
questions.ans: Missing the **closing quotation mark** (and the line is a syntax error).

questions.q: There are several **syntax errors** in this code. Write a corrected version.
questions.ans: **print("John is " + str(23) + " years old")** – matching quotes, str() for the number, one closing bracket.

questions.q: Find and fix **two** syntax errors.
questions.ans: Line 2: missing **colon**. Line 4: needs **+ str(total)**. Prints Total: 10

questions.q: This program should double the height. What does it actually do, and what type of error is it?
questions.ans: input() gives a **string**, so height*2 **repeats the text** (e.g. 180180): a **logic error**. Fix: int(height) * 2 and str().

questions.q: This loop should keep asking until the age is between 1 and 120. Syntax or logic error? Fix it.
questions.ans: **Logic error**: a number can't be < 1 **and** > 120, so the loop never runs. Use **or**.

questions.q: Give a **disadvantage** of binary search.
questions.ans: The list must be **sorted** first (and it is more complex to code).

questions.q: What is a **pre-requisite** for using binary search on an array?
questions.ans: The data must be **sorted** (in order).

questions.q: Why might you choose **linear** search instead of binary search?
questions.ans: The list is **unsorted**, or **small**; linear search is **simpler** to code.

questions.q: Which is the fastest search algorithm on **long, sorted** lists?
questions.ans: **Binary search**.

questions.q: I want to use binary search on **1, 4, 3, 9, 8, 2, 5** to find 8. What is the problem? What happens if I try?
questions.ans: The list is **not sorted**. Middle is 9: 8 < 9 so it searches the left half (1, 4, 3) and **never finds 8**.

questions.q: Put these sorting algorithms in order of efficiency on long lists, slowest first: **merge, bubble, insertion**.
questions.ans: **Bubble**, **insertion**, **merge** (fastest).

questions.q: Which sorting algorithm is the most efficient on long lists? What are its main drawbacks?
questions.ans: **Merge sort**. More **complex** to code and uses **more memory**.

questions.q: Give **two advantages** of bubble sort over merge sort.
questions.ans: **Simple** to code; **less memory**; quick to **check if a list is already sorted**.

questions.q: Give one **similarity** and one **difference** between bubble sort and insertion sort.
questions.ans: Both are **simple** and work **in place**. Bubble swaps neighbours in passes; insertion **inserts each item into a sorted part**.

questions.q: True or false: "Merge sort is always faster than bubble sort." Explain.
questions.ans: **False**: on a **small or nearly sorted** list, bubble sort can be as fast or faster.

questions.q: What are the **3 programming constructs**?
questions.ans: **Sequence**, **selection**, **iteration**.

questions.q: Which keyword(s) do we look for if an exam paper asks us to find **selection**?
questions.ans: **if** (elif, else, switch/case).

questions.q: Which keywords do we look for when asked to find **iteration**?
questions.ans: **for**, **while**, **do … until**.

questions.q: FOR, WHILE, DO…UNTIL. These instructions all signal what?
questions.ans: **Iteration**.

questions.q: On which line is: (a) the first selection (b) an empty list made (c) an item added to a list (d) a condition-controlled loop?
True or false: "A WHILE loop is an example of count-controlled iteration." Explain.
questions.ans: **False**: a while loop is **condition-controlled**; it repeats until a condition changes.

questions.q: What is the difference between a **variable** and a **constant**? Give an example of each.
questions.ans: A constant **cannot change** while the program runs (e.g. VAT_RATE = 0.2); a variable can (e.g. score).

questions.q: A program adds VAT to purchases. Should the VAT rate be a **variable** or a **constant**? Why?
questions.ans: **Constant**: it doesn't change while the program runs, and it only needs updating in **one place**.

questions.q: Write "**date of sale**" as a **camelCase** and a **snake_case** variable name.
questions.ans: **dateOfSale** and **date_of_sale**

questions.q: Write "**length of base**" and "**customer surname**" in snake_case and camelCase.
questions.ans: **length_of_base**, **lengthOfBase**, **customer_surname**, **customerSurname**

questions.q: What do we mean when we **increment** a variable? Write a line of Python that does it.
questions.ans: Increase it by a fixed amount (usually 1): **count = count + 1** (or count += 1).

questions.q: Write a line of Python to collect the user's **weight in kg** as a number.
questions.ans: **weight = float(input("Weight in kg: "))**

questions.q: Which of these is the operator for "to the power of" in Python?  ^  **  //  %
What is the symbol for MOD in Python, and what does it do?
questions.ans: **%** gives the **remainder** after division (e.g. 14 % 4 = 2).

questions.q: What will **print(5 ** (5 // 2))** output?
What is **140 // 60** and **140 % 60**? How might this be useful in real life?
questions.ans: **2** and **20**: 140 minutes is **2 hours 20 minutes** (converting units of time).

questions.q: What will this print?
questions.ans: **2, 4, 6, 8** then **Who do we appreciate?**

questions.q: What will this print? Write the first 6 lines.
What will this print?
questions.ans: **I love oranges** (only once).

questions.q: What is the difference between a **float** (real) and an **integer**?
questions.ans: An integer is a **whole number**; a float/real **can have a decimal part**.

questions.q: Define **casting**.
questions.ans: **Changing the data type** of a value, e.g. int("5") or str(42).

questions.q: Define **concatenation**. What error does it often cause in Python?
questions.ans: **Joining strings** together with +. Joining a string to a number causes a **TypeError** unless you use str().

questions.q: Best data type for: **number of children**, **height in metres**, **homeowner? (yes/no)**, **phone number**?
questions.ans: **Integer**, **real/float**, **Boolean**, **string** (leading 0, no maths).

questions.q: I am recording **rainfall in mm** each day to work out a weekly average. Which data type? Boolean, float, string or integer?
questions.ans: **Float (real)**: rainfall and averages can have decimals.

questions.q: What would be the best data type for someone's **postcode**? Why?
questions.ans: **String**: it contains letters, numbers and a space.

questions.q: I am recording customers' **names** in Python. What data type should I use?
questions.ans: **String**.

questions.q: word = "Henry". What is **word[0]**? What is **word[-1]**?
What will this output?
questions.ans: **hey**: song[1:3] is "he" and song[8] is "y".

questions.q: What will this output if the user enters **joe BLOGGS**?
questions.ans: **Hi Joe Bloggs**: .title() capitalises the first letter of each word.

questions.q: What kind of brackets are used for **lists** in Python?
questions.ans: **Square brackets** [ ].

questions.q: How do you check if an item is **in** a list in Python?
questions.ans: Use **in**, e.g. `if "cat" in pets:`

questions.q: What will be printed?
questions.ans: **Fox, Horse, Gerbil, Goldfish, Rabbit** (one per line), then **['Gerbil', 'Goldfish', 'Rabbit']**

questions.q: I have a **chessboard** (8 by 8 grid). I want to store the position of every piece. What data structure should I use?
questions.ans: A **2D array/list** (8 rows × 8 columns).

questions.q: What will this print?
questions.ans: **X**: row 1, column 1 is the centre.

questions.q: What are the **2 types of subprogram**? How are they different?
questions.ans: **Functions** return a value; **procedures** don't.

questions.q: Copy and complete: "There are two types of subroutine: ______ ______ data but ______ don't."
questions.ans: **Functions return** data but **procedures** don't.

questions.q: If a subroutine **returns** data, is it a function or a procedure?
questions.ans: A **function**.

questions.q: Give **3 benefits** of using subprograms / modular programming.
questions.ans: **Reuse** code; **easier to test** and debug; **easier to read/maintain**; can be **shared** between programmers.

questions.q: Which line contains a list? Which line is count-controlled iteration? What will the program print?
questions.ans: Line **3**; line **5**; prints **6** (5 letters + 1 for "q").

questions.q: What is in log.txt afterwards? What if it already had 10 lines?
questions.ans: **Run 0 / Run 1 / Run 2** on 3 lines. **"w" overwrites**, so the old lines are lost ("a" would append).

questions.q: Table **Customers** has fields CustomerName, Email, Town. Write SQL to show the **name and email** of customers in **Norwich**.
questions.ans: **SELECT CustomerName, Email FROM Customers WHERE Town = "Norwich"**

questions.q: What word beginning with "v" is the technique that stops users entering silly data?
questions.ans: **Validation**.

questions.q: Give **3 examples** of defensive design techniques.
questions.ans: **Input validation**, **authentication**, **anticipating misuse**, **maintainability** (comments, indentation, sensible names).

questions.q: Give **3 types** of input validation.
questions.ans: **Range** check, **type** check, **length** check, **presence** check, **format** check.

questions.q: Define **authentication** and give 2 ways it can be performed.
questions.ans: Checking a user **is who they say they are**: passwords, PINs, biometrics, two-factor codes.

questions.q: What is the difference between **validation** and **authentication**?
questions.ans: Validation checks data is **sensible**; authentication checks **who the user is**.

questions.q: What is the difference between **iterative** and **final** testing?
questions.ans: Iterative: **during development**, testing each part as it is made. Final: **at the end**, testing the whole program.

questions.q: An input must be text **between 4 and 8 characters**. Give valid, invalid and boundary test data.
questions.ans: Valid: **"cats1"** (5). Invalid: **"ab"** or 10 characters. Boundary: **4 and 8** characters (also 3 and 9).

questions.q: Draw an **AND** gate and its truth table.
questions.ans: D-shaped gate. Output 1 **only when both inputs are 1** (00→0, 01→0, 10→0, 11→1).

questions.q: Draw an **OR** gate and its truth table.
questions.ans: Curved gate. Output 1 when **at least one input is 1** (00→0, 01→1, 10→1, 11→1).

questions.q: Draw a **NOT** gate and complete its truth table.
questions.ans: Triangle with a circle. **1→0, 0→1**.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a **truth table**?
questions.ans: To show the **output for every possible combination of inputs**.

questions.q: How many rows does a truth table with **3 inputs** need (not counting headings)?
Give an **advantage** and a **disadvantage** of a low-level language like assembly language.
questions.ans: + **Fast** / direct control of hardware, small code. − **Hard to write and debug**; specific to one type of CPU.

questions.q: What are the advantages of a **high-level** language over a low-level language?
questions.ans: **Easier to read, write and debug**; **portable** between different machines.

questions.q: What job do interpreters, compilers and assemblers all do? How are they different?
questions.ans: All **translate** code to machine code. Compiler: whole program at once into an **executable**. Interpreter: **line by line**, stops at first error. Assembler: **assembly language** to machine code.

questions.q: Which **2 types of translator** generate an object code file (usually an .exe)?
questions.ans: **Compiler** and **assembler**.

questions.q: Python stops at the **first error** and runs line by line. Compiler or interpreter? Give one benefit of a **compiler** for selling a game.
questions.ans: **Interpreter**. Compiled code **runs faster**, hides the source code and needs no translator.

questions.q: Give **3 features** of an IDE.
questions.ans: **Editor** (autocomplete, colour-coding, indentation), **error diagnostics**, **run-time environment**, **translator**, **debugging tools**.

questions.q: Explain one way that using an IDE can help a programmer. (2 marks)
questions.ans: e.g. **syntax highlighting** makes errors easier to spot, **so** they are fixed before running.

questions.q: Name the **4 registers** in the CPU and say what each does.
questions.ans: **PC** (address of next instruction), **MAR** (address being read/written), **MDR** (data/instruction fetched or to be written), **ACC** (results of calculations).

questions.q: What does the **Control Unit** do?
questions.ans: It **decodes instructions** and **manages their execution**, sending control signals to other parts.

questions.q: What is the role of the **accumulator**?
questions.ans: It **stores the results of calculations** done by the ALU.

questions.q: Which CPU register holds the **data** coming from or going to RAM?
questions.ans: The **MDR** (memory data register).

questions.q: True or false: "The **MDR** is where the **address** of data to be fetched from memory is held." Explain.
questions.ans: **False**: the **MAR** holds the address; the MDR holds the data.

questions.q: What is a **bus** in the CPU?
questions.ans: A set of **wires along which data, addresses or control signals travel**.

questions.q: Match the CPU parts to their jobs: control unit, clock, ALU, cache, registers.
questions.ans: CU **decodes/manages**; clock **pulse to synchronise**; ALU **calculations and comparisons**; cache **fast memory for frequently used data**; registers **tiny storage locations in the CPU**.

questions.q: How is **main memory (RAM)** used in the fetch-decode-execute cycle?
questions.ans: Instructions and data are **fetched from RAM** (address via MAR, contents via MDR) and results may be **written back**.

questions.q: Describe the **fetch** stage of the FDE cycle.
questions.ans: PC address copied to **MAR**; **PC + 1**; instruction at that address copied to **MDR**, then to the CIR.

questions.q: What are the **3 Cs** of CPU performance? Explain how each affects speed.
questions.ans: **Clock speed** (more cycles per second), **cores** (more instructions at once), **cache** (less waiting for RAM).

questions.q: Quad core at **1.5 GHz** vs dual core at **2 GHz**. Which is faster? Explain.
questions.ans: **It depends**: the quad core is faster if software can use all cores; the dual core is faster for single-threaded tasks.

questions.q: True or false: "2 cores at 1 GHz will always be faster than 1 core at 1.2 GHz." Explain.
questions.ans: **False**: not all programs can **split tasks across cores**; then the faster single core wins.

questions.q: Define an **embedded system** and give an example.
questions.ans: A computer **inside a larger device** with a **dedicated function** (e.g. washing machine, microwave, car engine control).

questions.q: "RAM is volatile memory." True or false? Why?
questions.ans: **True**: RAM **loses its contents when the power is off**.

questions.q: Explain why **virtual memory** is needed and why it slows processing.
questions.ans: When **RAM is full**, part of **secondary storage** is used temporarily. It is slow because data must be **moved back to RAM** before it is processed.

questions.q: Which stores the **boot-up instructions**: RAM or ROM? Why can't the other do this?
questions.ans: **ROM**. RAM is **volatile**, so it would lose them when switched off.

questions.q: What are the **3 types** of secondary storage? Give an example of each.
questions.ans: **Magnetic** (hard disk), **optical** (DVD, Blu-ray), **solid state** (SSD, USB stick, SD card).

questions.q: Explain why computers need **secondary storage**.
questions.ans: RAM is volatile, so secondary storage **keeps data and programs when the power is off**.

questions.q: Name **2 magnetic** storage devices.
questions.ans: **Hard disk drive** and **magnetic tape**.

questions.q: Suggest a secondary storage device for a small business to **back up 2 PCs**. Justify it.
questions.ans: An **external HDD**: **cheap per GB**, high capacity, portable (or cloud).

questions.q: Which is faster, a hard disk or an SSD? Why might you still buy a hard disk?
questions.ans: **SSD** is faster. HDDs are **cheaper per GB** and have **larger capacities**.

questions.q: How many **bits** are in a byte? How many **nibbles**?
questions.ans: **8** bits; **2** nibbles.
questions.short: Bits and nibbles in a byte

questions.q: What is **half a byte** called?
questions.ans: A **nibble** (4 bits).

questions.q: How many **megabytes** are in a **gigabyte**?
What is a **character set**? Give 2 examples.
questions.ans: All the characters a computer can represent, **each with its own binary code**: **ASCII**, **Unicode**.

questions.q: How many bits per character in **ASCII**, **extended ASCII** and **Unicode**?
Why can't ASCII represent all the languages of the world?
questions.ans: 7 bits gives only **128 characters**: not enough for other alphabets and symbols. **Unicode** uses more bits.

questions.q: What benefits did **extended ASCII** and **Unicode** bring?
questions.ans: Extended ASCII: **256 characters** (accents, symbols). Unicode: **all world languages** and emoji.

questions.q: Define the term **pixel**.
questions.ans: The **smallest element (dot) of an image**; it shows one colour.

questions.q: What is **metadata**? Give 3 examples for an image.
questions.ans: Data about the data: **width, height, colour depth**, date taken, location, camera.

questions.q: If I decrease the **colour depth** of an image, what are 2 effects?
questions.ans: **Fewer colours** (lower quality) and a **smaller file size**.

questions.q: Draw this 5×5 image where 1 = white and 0 = black: 01110, 10101, 11011, 11011, 11011.
questions.ans: Row by row: shade each **0** black. (A simple face/house shape.)

questions.q: How is sound **captured and stored**? Use: analogue, wave, sampled, digital, binary.
questions.ans: The **analogue** sound **wave** is **sampled** at regular intervals; each sample's amplitude is stored as a **binary** number, making it **digital**.

questions.q: What is the formula for the **file size of a sound file**?
questions.ans: **sample rate × bit depth × length in seconds** (bits).

questions.q: If we **increase the sample rate** of a recording, what are the 2 effects?
questions.ans: **Better quality** (closer to the original) and a **larger file**.

questions.q: How could I **reduce the size** of a sound file? (2 ways)
questions.ans: Lower the **sample rate**, lower the **bit depth**, shorten it, or **compress** it.

questions.q: Give 2 benefits of **compressing** files.
questions.ans: **Less storage space**; **faster to send** over a network/email.

questions.q: Explain what we mean by **lossless** compression.
questions.ans: File is made smaller **without losing any data**; the original can be **fully restored**.

questions.q: A **text file** needs compressing. Which type of compression and why?
questions.ans: **Lossless**: losing data would **change or corrupt the text**.

questions.q: 20,000 old **photos** to back up. Lossless or lossy to save space? Why?
questions.ans: **Lossy** saves the most space and small losses are hard to see; **lossless** if every detail must be kept.

questions.q: A student stores 00100010 as the hex number **22** to save storage space. Are they right? Why?
questions.ans: **No**: hex is just an easier way for **humans** to read binary; it is **still stored as binary**.

questions.q: What is the difference between a **LAN** and a **WAN**?
questions.ans: LAN: **small geographical area**, own hardware. WAN: **large area**, uses **third-party** infrastructure (e.g. telecoms).

questions.q: Which type of network uses **switches**? Which uses **routers**?
questions.ans: Switches connect devices in a **LAN**; routers connect networks together (**WAN**/internet).

questions.q: What hardware is needed to connect **6 PCs** in a star LAN?
questions.ans: A **switch**, a **NIC** in each PC, and **cables** (Ethernet).

questions.q: Draw a **star** network with 3 PCs and a printer.
questions.ans: Every device connected by its own cable to a **central switch**.

questions.q: Draw a **full mesh** network with 4 PCs.
questions.ans: Every PC connected **directly to every other** PC (6 connections).

questions.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of a **mesh** network over a **star**.
questions.ans: + **No single point of failure**. − **More cabling**, more expensive.

questions.q: State **2 advantages** of a client-server model over peer-to-peer.
questions.ans: **Central backups** and **security**; files and software **managed in one place**.

questions.q: What is the main **benefit of using layers** in networking?
questions.ans: Each layer can be **developed/changed independently**; makes networks **easier to design and troubleshoot**.

questions.q: What is the difference between a **MAC address** and an **IPv4 address**?
questions.ans: MAC: **fixed, unique to the hardware** (NIC). IP: **assigned by the network**, can change; used for routing.

questions.q: Is **192.300.231.5** a valid IPv4 address? Why?
questions.ans: **No**: each number must be **0 to 255**, and 300 is too big.

questions.q: Which network protocol is used for **sending email**?
questions.ans: **SMTP**.

questions.q: Which protocol would be best for **gaming**? Why?
questions.ans: **UDP**: **faster**, no waiting for lost packets to be resent.

questions.q: What is a **brute force attack** and what threat would it pose to a school?
questions.ans: **Trying every possible password** until one works; could give access to **pupil data**.

questions.q: Why should you be wary of social media posts asking "What was your first pet's name?"
questions.ans: It's a **common security question**; answering gives attackers data to **guess or reset passwords** (social engineering).

questions.q: What is the difference between a **worm** and a **virus**?
questions.ans: A virus **attaches to a file** and needs a user to run it; a worm **spreads by itself** across networks.

questions.q: State **4 roles** of the operating system.
questions.ans: **Memory** management, **peripheral** management (drivers), **user** management, **file** management, user interface, multitasking.

questions.q: Which OS function deals with: (a) renaming a file (b) reading from a scanner (c) changing a login password?
questions.ans: (a) **file** management (b) **peripheral** management (c) **user** management

questions.q: What are the pros and cons of a **graphical user interface**?
questions.ans: + **Easy to learn**, intuitive. − **Uses more memory/processing**, slower for expert tasks than a CLI.

questions.q: What is the purpose of **utility software**? Give 2 examples.
questions.ans: Helps **maintain and protect** the computer: **defragmenter**, **compression**, **encryption**, backup.

questions.q: Utility or application? word processor, spreadsheet, disk defragmenter, compression program, web browser.
questions.ans: Applications: **word processor, spreadsheet, web browser**. Utilities: **defragmenter, compression**.

questions.q: Why does performance improve after a hard disk has been **defragmented**?
questions.ans: File parts are moved **next to each other**, so the read head **moves less** and reads faster.

questions.q: Name the **3 laws** you need to know. Give an example of how each could be broken.
questions.ans: **Data Protection Act** (keeping data too long), **Computer Misuse Act** (logging into an account without permission), **Copyright, Designs and Patents Act** (copying software).

questions.q: Which law requires companies to keep personal data **only as long as needed**?
questions.ans: The **Data Protection Act** (2018).
questions.short: Keep data only as long as needed

questions.q: A shop throws its **paper customer records** in a skip. Which law is it probably breaking? What should it do instead?
questions.ans: **Data Protection Act**: data must be kept **secure**; it should **shred** them.

questions.q: Someone uses a teacher's unlocked computer to look at **student records** and change some marks. Which law(s) have been broken?
questions.ans: **Computer Misuse Act** (unauthorised access and modification) and the **Data Protection Act** (personal data not kept secure).

questions.q: Give 2 benefits of **open source** software.
questions.ans: **Free**; can be **modified**; large community **improves and checks** it.

questions.q: All new phones must use **USB-C** for charging. What are the pros and cons?
questions.ans: + **Less e-waste**, one charger for all. − Less **innovation**, old chargers become waste.

questions.q: Give **4 environmental issues** connected with technology.
questions.ans: **E-waste**, **energy use** (data centres), **mining rare metals**, **pollution** from manufacturing/transport.

questions.q: Write a line of Python that stores a random whole number from **1 to 6** in a variable called **roll**.
questions.ans: **roll = random.randint(1, 6)** (after **import random**)

questions.q: Where should **import** statements go in your program? Why?
questions.ans: At the **top**, so the module is loaded **before** it is used.

questions.q: What is the job of a **DNS** server?
questions.ans: It turns a **domain name** (URL) into the matching **IP address**.

questions.q: Give an advantage and a disadvantage of **cloud storage** as a backup.
questions.ans: + **Off-site**, access anywhere, someone else maintains it. − Needs an **internet connection**; **security/privacy** relies on the provider.

questions.q: Apart from the world wide web, name **2 services** that run over the internet.
questions.ans: **Email**, **online gaming**, **video calls**, **file transfer (FTP)**, **streaming**.

questions.q: Give **3 ways** a school could protect its network from attack.
questions.ans: **Firewall**, **anti-malware**, **strong passwords/user access levels**, **penetration testing**, **encryption**, **staff training**.

questions.q: What is **penetration testing** and why do organisations use it?
questions.ans: Paying people to **try to break into** your own systems, to **find weaknesses before criminals do**.

questions.q: State the **smallest** denary number that can be represented by a **5-bit** binary number.
questions.misc: Giving 1 instead of 0.

questions.q: State the minimum number of bits needed to represent **100 different** characters.
questions.misc: Giving 2^100 or 128 (the number of values) instead of the number of bits.

questions.q: Describe how to convert a 2-digit hexadecimal number into denary. Use **3C** as your example.
questions.ans: Multiply the first digit by **16** and add the second: 3 × 16 = 48, C = 12, so **60**. (Or convert each digit to a nibble and then to denary.)

questions.q: Describe the binary shift that **multiplies** a number by **8**.
questions.ans: A **left** shift of **3** places (2³ = 8).
questions.misc: Giving 4 or 8 places.

questions.q: Describe the binary shift that **divides** a number by **4**. What can go wrong?
questions.ans: A **right** shift of **2** places. Bits shifted off the right are **lost**, so odd results are rounded down.

questions.q: Which is the same as **3 terabytes**? 3000 MB, 300 000 MB, 3 000 000 MB, 30 000 MB
Which is the **smallest**: 2 GB, 400 MB, 350 000 KB, 3 000 000 bytes?
In ASCII, **K = 01001011**. Write the binary code for **N**.
Give **one benefit** and **one drawback** of using **Unicode** instead of ASCII.
questions.ans: + Represents **more characters** (other alphabets, emoji). − Uses **more bits** per character, so files are **larger**.

questions.q: **4 images**, each **100 × 50 pixels**, colour depth **8 bits**. Calculate the total size in kilobytes. Show your working.
questions.misc: Forgetting to multiply by the number of images.

questions.q: Tick the correct description of **sound sampling**: (a) the frequency is measured each second (b) the **amplitude** is measured at **set intervals** (c) the digital wave is measured (d) the resolution is measured
questions.ans: **(b)** the amplitude of the wave is measured at set intervals
questions.misc: Saying the frequency is measured (frequency is the pitch).

questions.q: Explain how **increasing the bit depth** affects a sound file.
questions.ans: **More amplitudes/values** can be stored for each sample, so it is **closer to the original sound** (better quality), but the **file is bigger**.
questions.misc: Thinking bit depth means more samples per second (that is the sample rate).

questions.q: A photographer needs to carry **lots of large files** between home and work. Solid state or optical? Justify your choice.
questions.ans: **Solid state**: **large capacity**, **durable** (no moving parts), **small and portable**, **fast** to read/write.
questions.misc: Giving a choice with no justification, or justifying the other type.

questions.q: A **smart thermostat** has ROM and RAM. State **one item** stored in ROM and **one** stored in RAM.
questions.ans: ROM: the **boot-up program/firmware** that runs the device. RAM: **current temperature reading**, **target temperature**, timer settings.

questions.q: Explain why an **embedded system** like a microwave does **not** need virtual memory.
questions.ans: It runs **one fixed program** with **known, small** memory needs, so **RAM never fills up**.

questions.q: State the purpose of the **program counter**.
questions.ans: It holds the **address of the next instruction** to be fetched.
questions.misc: Thinking the PC counts how many programs have run or how many instructions have been processed.

questions.q: What does the **MAR** store? What does the **MDR** store?
questions.ans: MAR: the **address** of the memory location to read/write. MDR: the **data or instruction** fetched from (or to be written to) that address.
questions.misc: Saying the MAR or PC stores data rather than an address.

questions.q: State the purpose of the **accumulator**.
questions.ans: It stores the **result** of calculations/processes carried out by the ALU.
questions.misc: Saying it stores the calculations rather than the results.

questions.q: A café has **30 computers** in one building. Give **two** reasons it is a **LAN**, not a WAN.
questions.ans: **Small geographical area** (one site); the café **owns the hardware/infrastructure**.
questions.misc: Saying it is a LAN because of the number of computers. LANs and WANs are not defined by size.

questions.q: Describe the role of the **switch** in a star network.
questions.ans: It connects the devices and **sends data only to the device it is addressed to** (using the MAC address).
questions.misc: Confusing a switch with a hub (which sends data to all devices).

questions.q: Describe what is meant by a **mesh** topology.
questions.ans: Each device is connected to **(at least) one or more other devices**, so data can take **more than one route**; no central device.
questions.misc: Describing a central device or a client-server network.

questions.q: Give **one benefit** and **one drawback** of a **star** topology instead of a mesh.
questions.ans: + **Easy to add devices**; if one cable fails only that device is affected. − If the **switch fails**, the whole network fails.
Valid, **invalid** (256 > 255), **invalid** (5 groups), valid
questions.misc: Thinking 4 numbers are needed but missing that each must be 0–255.

questions.q: A school already has **wired** connections. Explain why it should **also** allow wireless.
questions.ans: Users can connect **mobile devices** (laptops, tablets) and **move around**; **more users** can connect without extra cables.
questions.misc: Saying wireless is cheaper (it is an extra cost on top of existing wiring).

questions.q: Describe how a URL is converted into an IP address.
questions.ans: The browser sends the URL to a **DNS server**; the DNS looks it up and **returns the IP address to the browser** (or passes the request to another DNS if not found).
questions.misc: Saying the URL goes to the web server, or that the IP address is sent to the user.

questions.q: Describe **two drawbacks** of storing a club's data in the **cloud**.
questions.ans: Needs an **internet connection** to access; relies on the **provider's security**; ongoing **cost**; less control over where the data is stored.

questions.q: Which OS function manages: (a) **multitasking** (b) **creating user accounts** (c) **installing a printer driver**?
questions.ans: (a) **memory** management (b) **user** management (c) **peripheral** management
questions.misc: Putting a printer driver under file or memory management.

questions.q: Explain the purpose of **encryption** software.
questions.ans: It **scrambles** data using a **key** so that **if it is intercepted it cannot be understood**.
questions.misc: Saying encryption stops data being intercepted (it doesn't; it stops it being understood).

questions.q: Fill the gap: "Defragmentation moves file parts to be ______ in storage so the read head moves less."
questions.ans: **consecutive** (next to each other)

questions.q: A gym stores members' personal data. **Name** the law it must follow and give **two** things it must do.
questions.ans: **Data Protection Act 2018**: keep data **secure**, **accurate/up to date**, only for the **stated purpose**, **no longer than needed**.
questions.misc: Describing what to do ("keep data safe") instead of naming the legislation.

questions.q: Tick **selection** or **iteration** for each keyword: **if**, **for**, **while**, **switch**
questions.ans: if = **selection**, for = **iteration**, while = **iteration**, switch = **selection**

questions.q: Identify and describe **two** types of iteration.
questions.ans: **Count-controlled** (for loop: repeats a set number of times). **Condition-controlled** (while / do until: repeats until a condition is met).
questions.misc: Calling a while loop count-controlled.

questions.q: State what is meant by a **syntax error** and give an example.
questions.ans: A mistake with the **rules/grammar** of the language, so the program **won't run/compile**, e.g. a **missing bracket** or misspelt keyword.
questions.misc: Giving only an example, not a definition.

questions.q: This should add **num1 and num2** and print "ok" for totals **from 10 to 20 inclusive**. Identify the **two logic errors** and correct them.
questions.ans: Line **3**: total = num1 + **num2**. Line **4**: if total >= 10 **AND total <= 20** then

questions.q: Complete the condition so it is True when **score** is from **1 to 100 inclusive**: `if score ____ AND ____ then`
questions.ans: `if score >= 1 AND score <= 100 then`
questions.misc: Writing "AND <= 100" without repeating the variable, which is not valid.

questions.q: word = "keyboard99". What is output by each? (a) `print(word.length)` (b) `print(word.upper)` (c) `print(word.left(3))` (d) `print(int(word.right(2)) + 1)`
In ERL, what does `"Broadland".substring(2, 4)` return?
questions.ans: **"oadl"**: start at index **2**, take **4** characters.
questions.misc: Treating the 2nd value as an end index (Python slicing) instead of a length.

questions.q: Write code that stores "Bure" in **a**, "Valley" in **b**, and joins them into **c** as "BureValley".
questions.ans: `a = "Bure"`, `b = "Valley"`, `c = a + b`
questions.misc: Using a comma (print(a, b)) which outputs two items but does not concatenate.

questions.q: How many times does this loop run? What is the last value printed?
questions.ans: **5** times (1 to 5 inclusive); last value **5**.
questions.misc: Assuming the end value is excluded, as in Python range().

questions.q: A do…until loop and a while loop both ask for a password. What is the key difference?
questions.ans: A **do…until** loop always runs **at least once** (checked at the end); a **while** loop checks **first** and might not run at all.

questions.q: This flowchart takes x, outputs "OK", then x = x − 2, and repeats until **x < 0**. How many times is "OK" output when x = **5**?
questions.ans: **3** times (x = 5, 3, 1; then x = −1 stops)
questions.misc: Off-by-one errors with < and 0.

questions.q: Complete the ERL to print every line of **scores.txt**.
questions.ans: `f = open("scores.txt")` … `while NOT f.endOfFile()` … `print(f.readLine())` … `endwhile` … `f.close()`

questions.q: Write a function **totalCost(tickets)** that **returns** the cost at **£12** per ticket.
questions.ans: `function totalCost(tickets)` / `return tickets * 12` / `endfunction` (Python: def … return tickets * 12)
questions.misc: Printing the result instead of returning it, or ignoring the parameter and asking for input inside the function.

questions.q: Write one line that calls **totalCost()** for **4 tickets** and stores the result in **price**.
questions.ans: `price = totalCost(4)`

questions.q: A linear search stops when the item is found. Identify **one other** condition that stops it.
questions.ans: It reaches the **end of the list** without finding the item.

questions.q: A bubble sort compares pairs of values and then… (a) always swaps (b) swaps if in the correct order (c) swaps if in the **incorrect** order
questions.ans: **(c)** swaps them if they are in the incorrect order

questions.q: Merge sort: how are two sorted lists combined?
questions.ans: Compare the **first item of each list**, move the smaller into the new list, repeat until both are empty.
questions.misc: Joining the two lists end to end and then sorting.

questions.q: Draw the logic circuit for **P = (A OR B) AND NOT C**.
questions.ans: A and B into an **OR** gate; C into a **NOT** gate; both outputs into an **AND** gate → P.
questions.short: Draw (A OR B) AND NOT C
questions.misc: Missing the circle on the NOT gate, or adding circles to AND/OR (that makes NAND/NOR).

questions.q: Identify and describe **two** IDE tools a programmer could use to build a program.
questions.ans: e.g. **editor** (write and edit code, with autocomplete/colour coding), **error diagnostics** (highlights errors), **run-time environment** (run and test), **translator**.
questions.misc: Naming language features such as comments or variables, which are not IDE tools.

questions.q: Give **two** ways to improve the **maintainability** of a program.
questions.ans: **Comments** to explain code; **meaningful variable names**; **indentation**; **subroutines**; constants.
questions.misc: Suggesting indentation when the code is already indented.

questions.q: Correct this SQL so it shows the **Name and Town** of every member in **Holt**.
questions.ans: `SELECT Name, Town FROM Members WHERE Town = "Holt"`
questions.misc: Using AND between fields, spaces in table names, IF instead of WHERE, and no quotes around text.

questions.q: Give the most suitable data type for each: **lapTime** = 59.8, **lapNumber** = 12, **finished** = True, **teamName** = "Rockets"
questions.ans: **Real/float**, **integer**, **Boolean**, **string**

questions.q: Input must be a whole number **1 to 50**. Is each normal, boundary, invalid or erroneous? **50**, **"fifty"**, **25**, **51**
questions.ans: 50 = **boundary**, "fifty" = **erroneous**, 25 = **normal**, 51 = **invalid**
